mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) being below 1.0% historically correlates with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as 70% of observations with FEDFUNDS < 1.0% yield positive returns.
evidence_refs: fact:70% positive return rate when FEDFUNDS < 1.0%
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 1.0%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in CPIAUCSL exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals accelerating inflation, historically causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to policy tightening expectations.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 3-month rises in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceeding 0.3pp each signal monetary tightening, historically producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise > 0.3pp in 3 months
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise > 0.3pp in 3 months, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), historical data shows negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to elevated discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of PAYEMS growth being above 0.5% in 3 months historically correlates with positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to strong labor market conditions supporting corporate earnings.
evidence_refs: fact:strong labor market supports equity returns
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in 3 months, the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month fall in HOUST exceeding 5% signals weakening housing demand, historically causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns due to reduced economic activity.
evidence_refs: fact:weakening housing demand causes negative returns
failure_condition: When HOUST falls > 5% in 3 months, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 3-month rises in HOUST and RSAFS exceeding 3% each signal strong consumer demand, historically producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.

evidence_refs: fact:strong consumer demand drives equity returns
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 3% in 3 months, the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply expansion regime (INDPRO growth > 2% in 3 months), historical data shows positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns due to improved economic output and corporate profitability.
failure_condition: When INDPRO growth > 2% in 3 months, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.
